questions.title: Interpreting an electron micrograph
questions.stem:
The electron micrograph includes a scale bar and one large organelle in section. A separate study counts inner-membrane profiles intersected by equal-length test lines placed at random in two muscle samples.

| Tissue | Total test-line length / µm | Intersections |
| --- | --- | --- |
| X | 40 | 48 |
| Y | 60 | 90 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the large organelle and give one visible feature supporting the identification.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate its maximum visible length relative to the scale bar and give the approximate length.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Compare the two normalized intersection counts. Why does the larger raw count alone not establish a difference in membrane density?

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain why the count alone does not establish a higher ATP synthesis rate in the intact tissue.

steps.text: It is a mitochondrion.
Internal folds consistent with cristae are visible inside the surrounding envelope.
The long dimension is roughly 2.5 scale bars (accept 2.3–2.8).
Each bar is 1.0 µm, so the length in section is about 2.5 µm with consistent measurement.
X=48/40=1.20 and Y=90/60=1.50 intersections µm⁻¹.
Y is 25% higher after normalization, but more total line length was sampled in Y.
The count provides a structural estimate whose interpretation depends on sampling and section orientation.
Actual synthesis also depends on factors such as oxygen availability, ADP supply and respiratory enzyme activity.

questions.title: Oxygen delivery under two conditions
questions.stem:
The table gives measured saturation of human haemoglobin at two pH values. For this model take oxygen capacity as 200 cm³ O₂ per dm³ fully saturated blood and neglect dissolved oxygen. Arterial blood begins at 97% saturation.

| Tissue oxygen partial pressure / kPa | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Saturation at pH 7.4 / % | 20 | 55 | 78 | 90 |
| Saturation at pH 7.2 / % | 12 | 40 | 65 | 83 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: At 4 kPa calculate O₂ unloaded per dm³ blood at each tissue pH.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Relate the change to respiration in an active tissue.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Blood flow in a muscle is 0.60 dm³ min⁻¹ at the lower pH. Estimate delivery to the tissue per minute and give two assumptions behind applying the calculation.

steps.text: At 7.4 the saturation drop is 97−55=42 percentage points, giving 84 cm³ dm⁻³.
At 7.2 the drop is 97−40=57 points, giving 114 cm³ dm⁻³.
The lower pH permits 30 cm³ more O₂ to unload per dm³.
Respiration produces CO₂, contributing to increased H⁺ and lower pH.
Lower pH reduces haemoglobin affinity for oxygen at a given partial pressure.
More oxygen is released where tissue oxygen demand is high.
Assume outgoing blood equilibrates with the specified tissue oxygen pressure and pH.
Assume the given inlet saturation and capacity are appropriate and flow is steady; accept another stated modelling assumption.

questions.title: Correcting a respirometer
questions.stem:
Equal-mass germinating seeds are in a respirometer with a CO₂ absorbent. A matched apparatus containing inert beads corrects for temperature and pressure changes. Displacement toward the chamber is positive. Calibration is 0.40 mm³ gas per mm displacement. Seed mass is 1.60 g.

| Time / min | 0 | 4 | 8 | 12 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Seeds / mm | 0 | 5 | 12 | 18 |
| Beads / mm | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate corrected oxygen uptake per gram per minute over 12 min.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain the role of the absorbent and the bead apparatus.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A second set at 30 °C has a higher corrected rate. State a suitable experimental improvement and explain why this result does not prove a higher ATP yield per oxygen molecule.

steps.text: Corrected displacement=18−3=15 mm.
Volume=15×0.40=6.0 mm³.
Respiration consumes O₂ and produces CO₂.
Removing CO₂ allows corrected gas-volume loss to represent oxygen uptake.
Beads reveal displacement caused by external pressure or temperature changes in the apparatus.
Use independent seed batches at each temperature and compare variability while holding mass and germination stage constant.
Uptake measures oxygen consumption rate, not directly ATP production.
ATP yield per O₂ also depends on coupling, so ATP production would need an independent measurement.

questions.answerSummary: Corrected displacement=18−3=15 mm.

questions.title: A test cross with unequal offspring counts
questions.stem:
A double heterozygote is crossed with a double recessive. Each recorded progeny class identifies the gamete contributed by the heterozygote. All progeny are sampled at the same stage.

| Gamete | MN | mn | Mn | mN |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Offspring | 184 | 196 | 66 | 54 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the likely parental arrangement and estimate the recombination frequency.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What counts would independent assortment predict, assuming equal survival? Use the observed pattern to assess that model.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain how crossing over makes the less common classes and give one reason the observed percentage need not equal the exact fraction of meiotic cells with any crossover.

steps.text: MN and mn are the most frequent, supporting MN/mn in the heterozygote.
Recombinant offspring=66+54=120 of 500.
Observed recombination=24%.
The expected ratio is 1:1:1:1, or 125 in each class.
Both parental classes exceed expectation while both recombinant classes fall below it.
The pattern supports linkage, although statistical testing and examination of survival bias strengthen the inference.
Non-sister chromatids of homologues exchange corresponding segments during prophase I.
An exchange between the two loci can produce Mn and mN combinations.
A crossover involves only two of four chromatids, and multiple crossovers can also restore parental marker combinations.

questions.answerSummary: MN and mn are the most frequent, supporting MN/mn in the heterozygote.
